te: Summary of 12 study sessions on Thai energy today and in the future
se: The committee considered its summary report on learning about Thai energy today and in the future, covering 12 study sessions with agencies, from the basics of electricity, the national energy plan, natural gas and price structures to energy diplomacy, with the key points and the committee's recommendations, to serve as policy proposals for energy reform.
it: Summary report on learning about Thai energy today and in the future

te: Waste to energy, and Thailand's fusion reactor
se: The renewable energy subcommittee heard the Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning on policy for turning waste into electricity (Waste to Energy). The electricity prices subcommittee planned to invite the ERC on removing power plants (factory type 88), and the hydrogen subcommittee planned to invite the Thailand Institute of Nuclear Technology on developing the Thailand Tokamak-1 fusion reactor.
it: Waste to Energy policy (Office of Natural Resources and Environmental Policy and Planning)
Removing power plants (factory type 88)
The Thailand Tokamak-1 fusion reactor

te: Studying energy diplomacy and the ASEAN Power Grid
se: The committee held a study session on Thailand's energy diplomacy policy and role, international energy cooperation and linking transmission grids in ASEAN (ASEAN Power Grid), with the agencies concerned explaining.
it: Study session on energy diplomacy and the ASEAN Power Grid

te: Waste power report outline, factory type 88, and options to lower power prices
se: The renewable energy subcommittee set the outline of its report on promoting community waste power plants. The electricity prices subcommittee heard the Department of Industrial Works on removing power plants (factory type 88) from the list annexed to the ministerial regulation under the Factory Act B.E. 1992, and considered its draft report on suitable options to lower electricity prices, such as natural gas resources and price structures. The hydrogen subcommittee reported a change of positions within it.
it: Outline of the report on promoting community waste power plants
Removing power plants (factory type 88) from the ministerial regulation list (Department of Industrial Works)
Draft report on suitable options to lower electricity prices

te: Studying the carbon credit market and the EU's CBAM
se: The committee held a study session on the carbon credit market and the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), such as how carbon credits are traded, the role of the Thailand Greenhouse Gas Management Organization, effects on exports and the shift to a green economy, with the agencies concerned explaining.
cre: Third Vice-Chair of the committee, presiding
it: Study session on the carbon credit market and CBAM

te: Community waste power plants, and dropping factory licences for power plants
se: The renewable energy subcommittee began studying policy to promote community waste power plants, starting with waste management in Thailand and overflowing urban waste. The electricity prices subcommittee planned to invite the Department of Industrial Works on cancelling factory operating licences (Ror.Ngor.4) for factory type 88 (power plants), and the hydrogen subcommittee planned to invite the Department of Rail Transport on using hydrogen in rail.
it: Policy to promote community waste power plants
Cancelling Ror.Ngor.4 licences for factory type 88 (power plants)
Using hydrogen in rail (Department of Rail Transport)

te: Studying the opening of the power sector, grid access and green electricity
se: The committee held a study session on opening up the electricity sector, such as the laws and policies involved, third party access (TPA) to the grid, wheeling charges and the utility green tariff (UGT), with the ERC and other agencies explaining.
it: Study session on opening the power sector, TPA, wheeling charges and UGT (ERC)

te: Electricity tariffs during unrest in the Middle East, and air pollution from transport
se: The renewable energy subcommittee heard the Department of Land Transport on vehicle registration figures and measures against air pollution from transport. The electricity prices subcommittee heard the ERC and EGAT on adjusting tariffs and managing fuel for power generation during the unrest in the Middle East, and the hydrogen subcommittee heard NSTDA on carbon standards and certification for hydrogen.
it: Measures against air pollution from transport (Department of Land Transport)
Tariffs and fuel management during the Middle East situation (ERC, EGAT)
Carbon standards and certification for hydrogen (NSTDA)

te: Studying hydrogen and small modular reactors (SMR)
se: The committee held a study session on hydrogen and small modular nuclear reactors (SMR), such as how they are produced, their benefits and limits, regulation and safety standards, with PTT Public Company Limited and the Thailand Institute of Nuclear Technology explaining.
it: Study session on hydrogen and SMR (PTT, Thailand Institute of Nuclear Technology)

te: Conclusions of the biomass report, natural gas prices and hydrogen for railways
se: The renewable energy subcommittee considered the conclusions and proposals of its report on renewable energy for clean air. The electricity prices subcommittee summarised information on the natural gas price structure, and the hydrogen subcommittee heard the State Railway of Thailand on preparing to use hydrogen in transport, as trains still run mainly on diesel.
it: Conclusions of the report on renewable energy for clean air
Summary on applying the natural gas price structure
Hydrogen for running trains (State Railway of Thailand)

se: The committee held a study session on electric vehicles and infrastructure, such as making Thailand a global production base for EVs, their competitiveness against other vehicles, charging stations and the obstacles involved, with the agencies concerned explaining.
it: Study session on electric vehicles and infrastructure

te: Biomass report proposals, natural gas pricing and hydrogen laws
se: The renewable energy subcommittee considered chapter 5, the proposals, of its draft report on clean air. The electricity prices subcommittee heard EPPO and the ERC on applying the natural gas price structure under the National Energy Policy Council's decision of 28 November 2025, and the hydrogen subcommittee followed progress on laws to regulate hydrogen as a fuel, safety standards for pipelines and hydrogen filling stations.
it: Proposals in the draft report on renewable energy for clean air (chapter 5)
Applying the natural gas price structure under the NEPC decision (EPPO, ERC)
Progress on laws for hydrogen and hydrogen filling stations

te: Studying energy storage, batteries and smart grids
se: The committee held a study session on energy storage systems (ESS) and smart grids, such as the battery industry and pumped-storage hydropower, with EGAT and other agencies explaining.
it: Study session on energy storage and smart grids (EGAT)

te: Studying renewable energy: solar, wind and waste
se: The committee held a study session on renewable energy in Thailand, such as rooftop and floating solar, wind and waste-to-energy, with DEDE explaining the draft Alternative Energy Development Plan 2024–2037 (AEDP2024), which aims for renewable energy to reach 37 per cent by 2037.
it: Study session on renewable energy and the draft AEDP2024 (DEDE)

te: Extending power lines to a village, and hydrogen production technology
se: The renewable energy subcommittee continued its draft report. The electricity prices subcommittee set a date to consider a complaint asking for power lines to be extended to a village in Prachuap Khiri Khan and another complaint, and the hydrogen subcommittee studied hydrogen technology, the country's production potential and its use in energy, industry and transport.
it: Draft report on renewable energy for clean air
Complaint asking for power lines to be extended, Prachuap Khiri Khan
Hydrogen technology and production potential in Thailand

te: The energy innovation testing project (ERC Sandbox) and plans to study hydrogen
se: The renewable energy subcommittee continued its draft report on clean air. The electricity prices subcommittee heard the ERC on its testing project for technology-based energy services (ERC Sandbox) phases 1 and 2, and the hydrogen subcommittee planned to invite the National Science and Technology Development Agency (NSTDA) to explain hydrogen technology.
it: Draft report on renewable energy for clean air
ERC Sandbox phases 1 and 2 (ERC)
Plan to study hydrogen technology (NSTDA)
